<div class="container page-wrap">

  <h2 class="section-heading">Open Positions</h2>

    <div class="col-md-4"><div class="join-track green"><div class="track-code">MS</div><h4>M.S. Students</h4><p>Master's students can pursue thesis or project-based research in PFAS remediation, water quality analytics, adsorbent characterization, and reactor design.</p><div class="note-box green">Research assistantships may be available depending on project fit and funding.</div></div></div>
    <div class="col-md-4"><div class="join-track purple"><div class="track-code">UG</div><h4>Undergraduate Researchers</h4><p>K-State undergraduates are welcome for independent study credit, paid research opportunities when available, or volunteer research experience.</p><div class="note-box purple">Students from engineering, agriculture, chemistry, environmental science, and related fields are encouraged.</div></div></div>

        <ul>

          <li>Interest in water treatment, soil remediation, materials, plasma, or analytical chemistry.</li>
          <li>Commitment to inclusive, collaborative research.</li>
          <li>Strong written and oral communication skills.</li>
          <li>Willingness to engage with agricultural and community stakeholders.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <div class="highlight-box">
        <h4>What We Offer</h4>
        <ul>
          <li>Hands-on training in advanced environmental treatment technologies.</li>
          <li>Interdisciplinary collaborations across K-State and partner institutions.</li>
          <li>Mentorship shaped by empathy, rigor, and professional development.</li>
          <li>Opportunities to present, publish, and connect research to real communities.</li>
          <li>A new lab culture that students will help build from the beginning.</li>
        </ul>

  <h2 class="section-heading">How to Apply</h2>
  <div class="info-panel apply-panel">
    <p>Prospective students and collaborators are encouraged to reach out before submitting a formal application. Email Dr. Choudhary with the subject line <em>Prospective [PhD/MS/UG] Student - [Your Name]</em> and include:</p>
    <ol>
      <li>A brief statement of your research interests and how they align with EC² Lab.</li>
      <li>Your CV or resume.</li>
      <li>Unofficial transcripts, if applying as a student.</li>
      <li>Contact information for 2-3 references, if available.</li>
    </ol>
    <a href="mailto:manisha.choudhary@ksu.edu?subject=Prospective%20Student%20-%20Your%20Name" class="btn-earth">Email Dr. Choudhary</a>
    <p class="small-note">For formal graduate applications, visit the K-State Biological and Agricultural Engineering graduate program.</p>
